q1_brood_parasites.query: birds that trick other species into raising their chicks
q1_brood_parasites.why_hard: The articles never say 'trick' or 'raising their chicks' — they say 'brood parasite' and 'lays its eggs in the nests of other birds'. Keyword search needs the literal words and finds nothing; dense semantic matches the meaning and surfaces the brood parasites (cowbirds, cuckoos).

required_spans.match_pattern: brood parasit|lays its eggs in the nests|host species

q2_mormon_crickets.why_hard: 'Mormon crickets' is a rare exact phrase that appears in just one article. Keyword search pinpoints it — the California gull, famous for devouring a plague of them — while dense semantic drifts to generic insect-eating birds and misses the gull entirely.

q3_pink_wading_bird.query: tall pink wading bird with long curved neck
q3_pink_wading_bird.why_hard: Articles rarely state 'pink' directly — the colour comes from the diet description elsewhere. Image cross-modal scores the appearance directly against stored bird photos.

query.semantic: What gives flamingos their pink color?

q4_flamingo_pink_color.user_query: what gives flamingos their pink color?
q4_flamingo_pink_color.why_hard: Coarse-to-fine. Plain BM25 returns the flamingo article but offers no way to drill into the relevant passage (the diet section explaining the colour). Dense visual finds pink birds but can't read prose. Two-stage retrieval — FTS gate + dense-text refine inside the candidate set — surfaces the passage that actually answers the question.

query.visual: black bird with bright spots on wings

q5_redwinged_blackbird_hybrid.user_query: a black bird with bright spots that swoops people in Illinois
q5_redwinged_blackbird_hybrid.why_hard: Visual-only lands on yellow-shouldered / tricolored blackbirds; text-only ignores appearance. Hybrid combines a hard $match_all text gate ('swoop' + 'illinois' must appear in body) with image-dense rerank to find the right bird.

q6_cardinal_eastern_feeders.query: Bright red songbird with a crest that visits backyard feeders in the eastern United States
q6_cardinal_eastern_feeders.why_hard: Three different facets — appearance (red + crested songbird), behavior (visits backyard feeders), region (eastern US). A single technique can only chase one facet at a time. The agent reads the whole question, routes each facet to the right tool, derives the arguments, and merges — so you don't have to decide the retrieval strategy up front.
